# JPEG 2000 fixtures

Everything in this directory is generated by `tests/oracle/gen_jp2.py` from synthetic images; nothing here is a
third-party file. `name.ext.ref` is what a reference decoder makes of `name.ext` (see the generator for which one),
`name.ext.<option>.ref` what `opj_decompress` returns with a decoder option (`-r`, `-l`, `-d`).

Encoders / decoders used by the generator:

* OpenJPEG 2.5.4 through python `imagecodecs` (and Pillow) - always.
* OpenJPH 0.32 through `imagecodecs` - always.
* The command line tools `opj_compress` / `opj_decompress` (OpenJPEG, BSD-2-Clause) and `ojph_compress` (OpenJPH,
  BSD-2-Clause) for what the python bindings do not expose. They are not installed system-wide; build them once:

      git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.5.4 https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg .tmp/opj-src
      cmake -S .tmp/opj-src -B .tmp/opj-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && make -C .tmp/opj-build -j
      git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/aous72/OpenJPH .tmp/ojph-src
      cmake -S .tmp/ojph-src -B .tmp/ojph-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && make -C .tmp/ojph-build -j

  (or point `OPJ_BIN` / `OJPH_BIN` at existing ones). Without them the generator leaves the affected fixtures alone.
* FFmpeg's own JPEG 2000 decoder for the component planes of one luma / chroma file (`sub_420_offset.j2k`).

The tests need none of these tools; they only use `imagecodecs` to decode what PixCodec's encoder writes, and
check less when it is missing.

## Conformance

The Rec. ITU-T T.803 | ISO/IEC 15444-4 (02/2024) decoder conformance test, class 1, may be used for conformance
testing only and is not in this repository: its list (`limits.txt`, with hashes and the error bounds of the standard)
and download script are in the test-data repository (see the README there), `Jp2ConformanceTests` runs it.
PixCodec passes all 65.
